sources.note: equipment plan source (research grade: datasheet); size 330 x 383 x 383 mm (w x d x h); port and control positions are placeholders until measured

Neumann KH 750 DSP page read 2026-11-12: "383 x 330 x 383 mm" (H x W x D), 19.5 kg, backplate: two electronically balanced XLR inputs, two electronically balanced XLR outputs (high-passed, a daisy chain for subwoofer arrays), one BNC input (75 ohm, AES3 or S/PDIF) and one BNC output (75 ohm, AES3), "a standard IP network connector" for MA 1 control, a universal switched-mode supply 100-240 V (the mains connector is not described), a 10 in long-throw woofer behind a black metal grille, sealed wood cabinet with an aluminium electronics panel; also a toggle switch for operation and calibration, input gain, output level, phase, low cut. Modelled: all eight connectors. Not stated: the XLR genders (convention: inputs female, outputs male), the network connector (RJ45 assumed) and the mains inlet (iec-c14 assumed): the plan row carries assumedConnectors net and power-in, both non-audio ports. The BNC pair is AES3 on 75 ohm BNC (aes3 signal). The page does not say the cabinet is rounded (radius 8 mm is our estimate). The `power` switch is the simulator power control, not the page's toggle. Positions are guesses.

Neumann rear photo (assets-source rear.webp, straight-on, 1600x1893). Cropped to the cabinet (aspect 0.863 against 330 x 383 mm) and read on a 20 mm grid: the four XLR (inputs left, outputs right) sit on one row at y 87 mm and x 76, 107, 139 and 171 mm; the BNC input and output at x 88 mm, y 165 and 145 mm; the RJ45 at x 138 mm, y 153 mm; the IEC inlet at x 258 mm, y 71 mm and the mains rocker above it at x 258 mm, y 96 mm. Positions +/- 3 mm. Only xMm and yMm changed; the openings, connectors and sizes are from the datasheet read above.
